paragraphs: An ongoing outbreak linked to alfalfa sprouts has sickened 76 people across 16 states, with 6 hospitalizations and no deaths reported [1]. The outbreak involves multiple strains of E. coli (O26:H11, O103:H25, and O168:H8) and Salmonella Agona [1]. In separate news, a Salmonella outbreak previously linked to jalapeños has ended; it affected 488 people across 34 states with 65 hospitalizations [2].

Inexport Logistics LLC is recalling YUPI GOLPE CON TODO SABOR BBQ mixed chips with chicharrón (pork cracklings) imported from Colombia in 60-gram foil bags as a Class I recall due to an import violation; the product was sold in Arizona, California, Colorado, Florida, Illinois, Kentucky, Minnesota, and Texas [3]. Stewart's Shops Corp. is recalling Heavenly Medley and Vanilla-Chocolate-Strawberry ice cream in half-gallon sizes due to potential metal contamination [4]. WinCo Foods is recalling Salsa Bean Dip Trays because they contain recalled peperoncini from G.L. Mezzetta [7]. Saint Francis Apizza LLC is recalling frozen pizzas in Pepperoni, Plain Cheese, Supreme, and Mushroom and Onion varieties due to undeclared soy allergens on labels [9].

Additional recalls include HOME GROWN Green Sprouting Calabrese Broccoli Seeds from EAK Distribution due to potential Salmonella contamination [5], expanded recalls of frozen organic berries from Great Value and Trader Joe's due to potential E. coli O145 contamination [6], and Sierra Nevada Cheese Company's Graziers Raw Milk Cheese due to potential E. coli O26:H11 contamination [12].
